body:
I found two bugs in `push_exchange_radiation_to_ice!`:
1. `-(fs.sic > 0) * fs.P_snow` compiles under CUDA to `(fs.sic > 0) * fs.P_snow` (the negated Bool loses its sign). GPU runs have therefore been getting negative snowfall, which would either drain snow or draw freshwater out of the ocean! **Fix**: just move the minus onto the Float.
2. The absorbed radiation was masked by `(sic > 0)` but not weighted by `sic`, so ice in partly covered cells absorbed `1 / sic` times the radiation it should. **Fix**: change `(sic > 0) *` to `sic *`.

This PR also adds a test to ensure these bugs are caught in the future (it checks the cell-mean heat flux and the snowfall for a simple setup). I don't know if it's really necessary or not; happy to remove it if we think it just adds bloat.
title: Fix snowfall and radiation on sea ice

body:
Adds a new `ocean_3d_diagnostic_interval` config flag that just defaults to `ocean_diagnostic_interval` used by the (2D) surface output. Useful if you want to output the surface diagnostics at a high frequency without wasting tons of memory on the 3D fields.

Also gives each writer its own file-splitting `TimeInterval` (the two writers shared one stateful interval).
title: Seperate output interval for 3D ocean diags
